chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh that he wrote to Abu al-Hasan (AS) asking him

about Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Did He have knowledge of things before He created them and their existence, or did He not know that until He created them and willed their creation and formation, so He knew what He created when He created it and what He formed when He formed it?'
He (AS) wrote in his own handwriting: 'Allah remained knowing of things before He created them, just as His knowledge of things after He created them.'
ai.seo_question: Is Allah's knowledge of creation eternal or did it begin when He created?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) affirms that Allah’s knowledge is an eternal attribute of His essence, not contingent upon the existence of created things, thereby refuting the notion that God acquires knowledge over time. This establishes the principle of *Qidam* (antiquity) of divine attributes, a cornerstone of Shia theology against the Mu'tazilite view of *Hadith al-Sifat* (acquired attributes). The Imam’s concise response underscores that divine knowledge is unchanging and identical in its nature before and after creation, emphasizing God’s absolute self-sufficiency.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 13. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ayyub ibn Nuh that I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Naqi (AS) asking him
about Allah, the Mighty and High: “Did He have knowledge of things before He created them or did He know them only after He created them?”
He (AS) wrote in his own handwriting: “Allah’s knowledge of things was the same before He created them and after He created them.”
